reasons.A: Modern, plain expository voice with short even sentences, no semicolon-balanced clauses, dashes or homely period similes; reads as a present-day critic, not the author.
reasons.B: Closest match: long sentences balanced on semicolons and '--' asides, confident Victorian assertion leavened with homely concrete touches (eating, sweating, the reckoning), and a string-and-beads close that echoes the author's easy figurative turn without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Right period register and semicolon rhythm, but piles on rhetorical questions, 'nay', and ornate similes the passage never uses, so it reads as a thicker imitation of the voice rather than the author.
